answers: where each of the 141 stage-2 opcodes sends the command pointer, and on what evidence

0x01.note: tools/walk_stream.py's DYNAMIC text records only the ctx[2]==0 arm, where the handler writes no pointer and returns 2; the ctx[2]!=0 arm at 0x8006db44-0x8006db7c does write ctx+0x1c, from the slot 0x18 saves. This entry records that arm rather than the note's 'no pointer write at all'.

0x03.note: the write is in the callee FUN_8006d5dc (0x8006d624), which the handler calls at 0x8006dba8; the index is byte 3 of the command.

0x07.name: ElseStart
0x07.note: published 4 is the command's own size; the handler's only ctx+0x1c write is the skip target computed from the u16 at byte 2 (0x8006dc84 lhu v0,2(v1) -> 0x8006dc8c addu v1,v1,v0), so this ElseStart has no constant path to walk by.

0x0d.name: ForStart
0x0d.note: resolve() reports [6, 12] and 12 is the trap: the scan carries a3 = cmd+6 out of the fall-through arm (0x8006de50) into the loop-exit arm, where 0x8006dea4 lh t0,2(a3) -> 0x8006dea8 addu v0,a3,t0 -> 0x8006deac addiu v0,v0,6 -> 0x8006deb0 sw v0,28(t2) is one variable path. The arms are the two sides of 0x8006de30 beq v0,zero, so the second advance is a skip of s16[cmd+2]+6, never a 12.

0x0e.name: LoopWhile
0x0e.note: the counter-expiry arm advances 2 at 0x8006dfcc; while the counter is non-zero the handler re-points ctx+0x1c at the block-start slot ctx+0x20 (0x8006dfb8 lw v0,32(v0) with the store in the 0x8006dfbc j delay slot), which is a loop back to a recorded target, not a length.

0x0f.note: the constant 4 is the block body; the second write restores the block end saved at iVar6+0x60 on the arm where the condition function FUN_8006e1bc returns 0, so the M154 override of the advance scan to 4 needs this second path recorded beside it.

0x10.note: a block return: the pointer comes back from the per-thread slot ctx+0x20, at an index that is itself read out of the context (s8[ctx+s8[ctx+2]+8]), so no operand of the command names it.

0x12.note: the constant 2 is the header advance; on the arm where FUN_8006e1bc returns non-zero the handler re-points ctx+0x1c at the block-start slot ctx+0x20 instead.

advances.expression: cmd + 4, scanned by entry + u16[entry+2]; exit entry + 2 (tag 0x15) or entry + 6 (case match)

0x13.name: Switch
0x13.note: resolve() reports 14, which is the linear scan chaining the tag-exit's cmd+6 (0x8006e2f8) with the 6-byte loop stride (0x8006e310) and the tag exit again (0x8006e320). A case-table scan has no single constant, and published 4 is the header, so Switch claims no constant advance at all.

0x17.name: Goto
0x17.note: published 6 is the command's own size; the only ctx+0x1c write is the computed target, stored in the jr ra delay slot at 0x8006e3d0 (0x8006e3a4 lh t0,4(a1) -> 0x8006e3bc addu a1,a1,t0), so Goto has no fall-through to walk by.

0x18.name: GoSub
0x18.note: published 2 is the command's own size; the handler also saves cmd+2 into ctx+0x144+idx*4 at 0x8006e3f0, which is the slot 0x19 and 0x01 pop, and then sets the pointer from the script table *(0x80114f2c) + u16[cmd+1].

0x19.note: pops the slot 0x18 pushes (ctx+0x144+idx*4) and reloads ctx+0x140 from the frame at 0x8006e480.

0x1a.note: block return from the ctx+0x60 end slot that 0x0d, 0x0f and 0x1b write.

0x1b.note: same shape as 0x0d and the same trap: resolve() reports [6, 12] because the scan carries a3 = cmd+6 out of the fall-through arm (0x8006df00) into the loop-exit arm (0x8006df60 lh t0,2(a3) -> 0x8006df68 addiu v0,v0,6 -> 0x8006df6c sw v0,28(t2)). The licensed table has no entry for this number, so the name stays null.

0x36.note: retracted in M226, twice over. The dispatch is `jr *(0x800b98e0 + (u16[cmd+4] >> 8)*4)` with the index bounds-checked against 5 -- at 0x800b98e0, not the 0x800c98e0 this file published, which is what `addiu v0,v0,-26400` gives if its immediate is read unsigned (it is -0x6720, so the base is 0x10000 lower). And the target is not a callback: the five entries are five arms of one dispatch, each selecting a base object before a shared tail computes three coordinates, calls FUN_80077adc and writes ctx+0x1c = cmd+12. So the advance is the constant 12 and the index selects a sub-opcode. Measured by tools/callback_table.py; the base objects the arms select *are* runtime-initialised, which is where that reading belongs.

refuses: a folded constant as a constant, a length for the six dynamic opcodes, any scheduler claim, and any name the inputs do not give
